title: [Request for feedback] Starlette/ASGI Support in Streamlit
body:
Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we're introducing experimental support for running Streamlit with [Starlette](https://www.starlette.io/) as the underlying web framework. This is the first step toward our long-term goal of **fully migrating from Tornado to Starlette/ASGI**, and we need your help to identify any issues or gaps before the full transition. ## What's New > **Note:** To use the experimental Starlette features, you need to install the optional dependencies: > > ```bash > pip install streamlit[starlette] > ``` ### 1. Starlette Server Mode (Experimental) You can now run Streamlit using Starlette instead of Tornado by setting a config option: ```toml # .streamlit/config.toml [server] useStarlette = true ``` Or via command line: ```bash streamlit run app.py --server.useStarlette=true ``` ### 2. ASGI App Entry Point (Experimental) For advanced use cases, you can now create an ASGI-compatible Streamlit application using the new `App` class: ```python from streamlit.starlette import App app = App("main.py") ``` Run it with `streamlit run` (preferred): ```bash streamlit run myapp.py ``` Streamlit will automatically detect the `App` instance and run it in Starlette mode. Alternatively, you can use any ASGI server directly: ```bash uvicorn myapp:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8501 ``` The `App` class supports advanced configuration including: - **Custom HTTP routes** — Add REST API endpoints alongside your Streamlit app - **Middleware** — Add security headers, authentication, logging, etc. - **Lifespan hooks** — Run code on startup/shutdown (e.g., pre-warm caches, initialize resources) - **Framework integration** — Mount Streamlit inside FastAPI, Django, or other ASGI frameworks > 📖 For more details on the `App` interface and its full capabilities, see the [specification in PR #13449](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13449).
Example: Adding custom routes ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.routing import Route from starlette.responses import JSONResponse async def health_check(request): return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy", "service": "streamlit-app"}) async def get_data(request): return JSONResponse({"items": ["apple", "banana", "cherry"], "count": 3}) app = App( "main.py", routes=[ Route("/api/health", health_check), Route("/api/data", get_data), ], ) ```
Example: Adding custom middleware ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware): async def dispatch(self, request, call_next): response = await call_next(request) response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff" response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "SAMEORIGIN" return response app = App( "main.py", middleware=[Middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)], ) ```
Example: Mounting FastAPI in Streamlit ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from starlette.routing import Mount from streamlit.starlette import App # Create FastAPI sub-application api = FastAPI() [USER].get("/health") async def health(): return {"status": "healthy"} [USER].post("/predict") async def predict(data: dict): return {"prediction": data.get("value", 0) * 2} # Mount FastAPI into Streamlit app # - Streamlit UI at / # - FastAPI endpoints at /api/* # - FastAPI docs at /api/docs app = App( "dashboard.py", routes=[Mount("/api", app=api)], ) ```
Example: Mounting Streamlit in FastAPI ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from streamlit.starlette import App # Create the Streamlit sub-application streamlit_app = App("dashboard.py") # Create FastAPI with Streamlit's lifespan to manage the runtime lifecycle api = FastAPI(lifespan=streamlit_app.lifespan()) [USER].get("/api/data") async def get_data(): return {"data": [1, 2, 3]} # Mount Streamlit under /dashboard api.mount("/dashboard", streamlit_app) # Run with: uvicorn myapp:api ```
Example: Lifespan hooks for startup/shutdown ```python from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from streamlit.starlette import App [USER] async def lifespan(app): # Startup: runs before accepting connections print("🚀 Starting up...") model = load_ml_model() # Pre-warm caches db = init_db_connection() # Yield state accessible via app.state yield {"model": model, "db": db} # Shutdown: cleanup resources print("👋 Shutting down...") db.close() app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan) ```
## Why We're Migrating to Starlette/ASGI The migration to Starlette/ASGI will unlock numerous frequently-requested features: ### Custom HTTP Endpoints - #439 - #9673 - #6195 - #9090 - #11333 - #8713 ### Security Headers & Middleware - #6417 - #9160 - #861 - #8823 ### Framework Integration & ASGI Support - #4311 - #4567 - #927 - #7546 ### Server Configuration & Lifecycle - #7688 - #8991 - #6108 - #9916 - #8545 - #7667 - #11050 - #10543 - #3426 - #8661 ### SEO & Metadata - #5673 - #8999 ### Advanced App Execution - #4162 - #9450 - #12972 - #662 ## We Need Your Feedback Since we plan to eventually make Starlette the default (and only) server backend, we want to catch any compatibility issues early. Please help us by: ### 1. Try it out Enable Starlette mode in your existing apps: ```bash streamlit run your_app.py --server.useStarlette=true ``` ### 2. Report any issues If you encounter problems, please comment below with: - **What happened** — Error messages, unexpected behavior - **Your environment** — OS, Python version, Streamlit version - **How to reproduce** — Minimal code example if possible - **Comparison** — Does the issue occur with the default Tornado server? ### 3. Share your use cases We're especially interested in: - ⚡ Performance comparisons (response times, memory usage, concurrent users) - 🔌 Integration scenarios (FastAPI, Django, other ASGI frameworks) - 🛡️ Security/middleware requirements - 🚀 Deployment configurations (uvicorn, gunicorn, hypercorn, cloud platforms) ## Known Limitations - This is **experimental** — APIs may change before the final release - TBD --- **Thank you for helping us build a better Streamlit!** Your early feedback is invaluable in ensuring a smooth transition for the entire community. 🙏 Please comment below with your experiences, questions, or concerns. ![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-13600)

Great job... I've tested some of the apps, and these are working fine, except I've got a small warning while starting the app on Windows:

[USER] This looks like it comes from our component v2 manager logic. Is your app using a custom component v2? This looks a bit more like an issue in our component v2 scanner, not necessary related to Starlette cc [USER] 

<details>
<summary>Claude analysis on this issue</summary>

# Summary                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                         
  This is a **bug in the components v2 `manifest_scanner.py`**, not specifically Starlette's fault.                      
                                                                                                                         
  ## The Issue                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                         
  Looking at `lib/streamlit/components/v2/manifest_scanner.py:191`:                                                      
                                                                                                                         
  ```python                                                                                                              
  def _is_likely_streamlit_component_package(                                                                            
      dist: importlib.metadata.Distribution,                                                                             
  ) -> bool:                                                                                                             
      # ...                                                                                                              
      name = dist.name.lower()  # <-- BUG: dist.name can be None                                                         
  ```                                                                                                                       
  The dist.name attribute from importlib.metadata.Distribution can be None in edge cases:                                
                                                                                                                         
  - Corrupted or malformed package metadata                                                                              
  - Certain editable installs                                                                                            
  - Packages installed in unusual ways                                                                                   
                                                                                                                         
  When dist.name is None, calling .lower() on it throws:                                                                 
                                                                                                                         
  'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lower'                                                                             
                                                                                                                         
  Why Starlette Triggers It                                                                                              
                                                                                                                         
  Starlette itself isn't the problem, but it likely:                                                                     
                                                                                                                         
  1. Has a dependency installed in a way that produces a distribution with None name                                     
  2. Or one of its transitive dependencies has malformed metadata                                                        
                                                                                                                         
  The scan iterates over all installed distributions via importlib.metadata.distributions(), so any broken package in the
   environment can trigger this.                                                                                         
                                                                                                                         
  The Fix                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                         
  The code should guard against None before calling .lower(). A simple fix would be:                                     
   
  ```python                                                                                                              
  def _is_likely_streamlit_component_package(                                                                            
      dist: importlib.metadata.Distribution,                                                                             
  ) -> bool:                                                                                                             
      # Skip distributions without a name                                                                                
      if dist.name is None:                                                                                              
          return False                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                         
      name = dist.name.lower()                                                                                           
      # ...                                                                                                              
 ```
                                                                                                     
  There are also other places in the file that use dist.name (lines 238, 510) that should be similarly guarded, though   
  they're only reached after the filtering function passes, so fixing line 191 would prevent most issues. 

</details>

Late last year, we did encounter some performance pressure due to a rapid increase in users (primarily due to those ~41 concurrent users handling real-time data exchange, introduced as part of a new feature). The experimental Starlette support helped significantly in handling that load. For reference, below are two snapshots from Cloudflare's analytics. Both views are configured to show **direct access only** (excluding page-to-page navigation) over a **24-hour period**. The data was captured at approximately **08:00 (local time)**. Hi [USER] This feature looks promising, and I'm excited to see the progress being made! However after upgrading Streamlit to v1.57.0, I encountered an issue with my Streamlit setup under bazel. Bazel replicates the directory structure during the build process by creating a real folder tree but symlinking every individual file to its actual location in the cache to save disk space. This behavior applies to the static frontend files bundled with the Streamlit library. Here is an example of the directory structure generated by Bazel: ```bash # The 'static' folder is real, but files inside are symlinks $ ll ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/ Permissions Size Date Modified Name ... lrwxr-xr-x@ - 21 Apr 15:39 file_util.py -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/file_util.py drwxr-xr-x@ - 21 Apr 15:39 static $ ll ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/ Permissions Size Date Modified Name lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 favicon.png -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/favicon.png lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 index.html -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/index.html lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 manifest.json -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/manifest.json drwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 static ``` ## The Problem The Starlette router used for serving Streamlit’s static files returns a 404 error because the default configuration for Starlette’s `StaticFiles` does not follow symlinks. Since the actual files reside outside the perceived "root" directory in the Bazel sandbox, Starlette blocks access to them for security reasons. ## Proposed Solutions After looking into the codebase, I believe there are two viable options to resolve this. (Details at the bottom.) ### 1. Set `follow_symlink = True` for `_StreamlitStaticFiles` `_StreamlitStaticFiles` inherits from `starlette.staticfiles.StaticFiles`. We can explicitly set the `follow_symlink` parameter to `True` in the constructor. Location: ```python # Proposed change super().__init__(directory=directory, html=True, follow_symlink=True) ``` This may have security implications as it allows serving files outside of the specified directory if there are symlinks pointing to them. However, since the static files are bundled with the Streamlit library and nothing else, this should not be a concern in this case. ### 2. Resolve the Static Files Path in `get_static_dir()` Streamlit's static directory path is determined by `get_static_dir()` function which is calculated relative to `file_util.py` location. Since `file_util.py` is also a symlink in the Bazel environment, we can resolve the physical path using `os.path.realpath` before passing it to the handler. Location: ```python def get_static_dir() -> str: """Get the folder where static HTML/JS/CSS files live.""" dirname = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)) # `realpath` instead of `normpath` return os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dirname, "static")) ``` Note: The result of this function is passed to `create_streamlit_static_handler` as `directory=`. I understand that Bazel support might not be a primary focus for the project, but addressing this would significantly improve compatibility for users in monorepo and containerized environments. Thank you for taking the time to read through this long report. I wanted to provide as much context as possible to make it easier to evaluate.
Details: Code I used to check that both approaches work. I tested both options with the following code. Commenting out both would result in 404 but if I enable one of the options, streamlit behaves as expected. ```python import os from pathlib import Path import streamlit as st from starlette.staticfiles import StaticFiles from streamlit import file_util from streamlit.web.server.starlette import starlette_static_routes PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.resolve() ### 1. Set `follow_symlink = True` for `_StreamlitStaticFiles` create_static_handler = starlette_static_routes.create_streamlit_static_handler def monkeypatch_create_static_handler(directory: str, base_url: str | None) -> StaticFiles: """Wrapper.""" print(f"Creating static handler for directory: {directory}, base_url: {base_url}") result = create_static_handler(directory, base_url) result.follow_symlink = True return result starlette_static_routes.create_streamlit_static_handler = monkeypatch_create_static_handler ### 2. Resolve the Static Files Path in `get_static_dir()` get_static_dir = file_util.get_static_dir def monkeypatch_get_static_dir() -> str: """Wrapper.""" dirname = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(os.path.normpath(file_util.__file__))) return os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dirname, "static")) file_util.get_static_dir = monkeypatch_get_static_dir app = st.App( PROJECT_ROOT / "main.py", debug=True, ) ```
[USER] Thanks for reporting this issue. I did a quick investigation, and I think it's fine to support this in Starlette via `follow_symlink=True`.
